recipes.name: Easy Corn Salsa
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro, or more to taste
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice, or to taste
salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Stir corn, bell pepper, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice, honey, crushed red pepper, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. For best flavor results, chill until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Corn Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This colorful corn salsa is simple to make in minutes with canned or fresh corn, bell pepper, jalapeño, red onion, cilantro, and lime juice.

video.description: Elevate your flavor game with our quick and delicious tutorial on how to make Easy Corn Salsa! In this mouthwatering video, we guide you through the simple steps to create a vibrant homemade corn salsa bursting with fresh ingredients. From sweet corn to zesty tomatoes and aromatic herbs, this easy-to-follow recipe guarantees a flavorful sensation perfect for any occasion.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is great! I added more lime juice, cilantro, and a red pepper to give it a stronger flavor and more color. I made it as a side to my main dish for the night and my boyfriend and I loved it so much we couldn't stop eating.

Brought to a Gathering of Friends. Used fresh corn from the cob (3 ears), Used 1/2 Red Onion added rinsed black beans (2 cans) Replaced honey with Light Blue Agave (4tbl). Squeezed juice of 2 Limes over entire mix Chopped Cilantro (more than recipe calls for, but no exact amt) Followed recipe otherwise with remaining ingredients. Everyone raved about it. Sorry, kinda made it my own with base recipe Will bring to future Friends Gatherings

refreshing! I left out the jalapeno and only used 1/2 an onion, used an entire lemon, and made it a little special by adding some shrimp (cooked quickly on a pan with a little oil and then cut into small pieces). Had it with pita bread for a light lunch.

This recipe is a hit with the family. We have had it on fish and chicken as well as with tacos and fajitas. I added a can of black beans, use the juice of a whole lime and used only half of the onion since they have been very hot.

Refreshing side that would go well with Mexican dishes, fish or by itself. I'll have to go light-handed on the crushed red pepper, as it had too much of a bite for me. It definitely needs the honey to offset all of the spiciness. I used a steamed, fresh ear of corn that equaled about the same amount in the can mentioned. The fresh cilantro from a plant I purchased recently worked nicely.

I'm rating this 5 stars because, if you make it to taste the way YOU like it, it's worth it.
It's not 5 stars as written (more like 3) because, even though she said she didn't measure, 1 whole onion and 1 whole pepper are too much for 1 can of corn. 
Here's what I used and I think it will be awesome after the flavors meld overnight (but it tastes great now):
1 can no sugar or salt added corn (I don't normally buy this kind, but I wanted to season the salsa to my liking)
1/4 of a large red bell pepper, diced small
1/4 of a medium sweet onion (didn't have red), diced small
1/2 of a medium jalapeno pepper, seeds removed, minced (might use more next time)
Approx 1 tsp crushed red pepper (didn't measure this)
2 tbsp chopped cilantro
Juice of 1/2 lime
Approx 1 tsp light blue agave (don't have honey)
Kosher salt & fresh cracked pepper to taste
After tasting it, as much as I love onion (even raw), I decided to add 1/2 Can of black beans (rinsed and drained) to mellow out the onion a bit.
I'm looking forward to eating this tomorrow because I think it is going to taste light and refreshing with a bit of heat - perfect for summer and July 4th weekend. Enjoy!

I made it and it was a huge hit. I used left over fresh corn and about a half a can chopped green chili's instead of cilantro. I also doubled the honey, but I had also used large onion, red pepper, and a great big jalapeno! We had it with pork carnita's and a pot of pint beans, man o man!

Delish! What a breath of spicy freshness… I did tweak mine to include double the cilantro, double of the honey & lime, of which I used lemon for lack of lime, half of small red onion, and I used a full jalapeño with seeds, thus omitting the need for red chili flakes. I also sprinkled some cotija on top. It was fantastic and gone in no time. Saving this one!
I didn’t have a orange pepper, but I used a red jalapeño and a green jalapeño. I used 3 ears of sweet dot fresh corn.I boiled the corn then cut off the kernels.

This is a great easy recipe! I have never made corn salsa before so wasn't sure if I would like it.I did change it a little with variations of 1/4 c yellow onion (didn't have a red),1/2 can black beans rinsed and drained,1 teaspoon sugar (didn't have any honey), 2 Tablespoons lime juice, 1 Tablespoon cilantro spice,& 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes.I took it to work and my co-workers loved it. Great with chips,or to use to cook chicken or salmon on the grill. The leftover I used on top of my turkey tacos!

I made this with (ok, more like I did the work and he stirred the ingredients) my bf for a potluck at his work. I just got a text that said "everyone loved it, you did good!" (lol) I just made a few tiny changes: 1) subbed red pepper for orange 2) added half a can of black beans 3) used closer to two tbs lime juice 4) subbed a chili pepper for jalapeno (what we had) 5) subbed garlic salt for regular salt. THANKS FOR SHARING! :)
It was on point but I added a couple of cans of rotel and more of each ingredient to make a larger size. Plus I added black beans (a can rinsed) as well.

This was the perfect side for taco night with the exception of a few ingredients. My hubby has geographical tongue so any strong spices cause a flare up. I didn’t include jalepeno, crushed red pepper or cilantro (personal preference). I added mild diced tomatoes with green chilis and about a teaspoon and a half of chili powder. Hubby was super happy and definitely will be making again, especially for family events!
This is so good and easy to make! I increased the lime juice dressing ingredients and next time I will use less onion, but that's just personal taste.
Have made this recipe a few times, such a terrific recipe. Made no changes to the ingredients.
I used a little less jalapeño and added a dash of cumin. It’s a great recipe though!
This is a great salsa. I did add one can of black beans.
I love corn (born in Iowa) and this was yummy. Doubled the lime juice and honey, and cut back on the onion. Thought it didn’t have a salsa texture to it so have been using as a salad with lunches! 👍
